newhire_tom: Hey all — first day! 🥳 Trying to bootstrap my dev env on an M2 MacBook Air. I installed Homebrew and asdf but when I run `python` or `node` I get `command not found`. My dotfiles are pretty minimal. Any standard PATH lines or asdf sourcing I should add? Do I need Rosetta for anything?

lena: welcome! For Apple Silicon the usual Homebrew prefix is /opt/homebrew, so add that to your PATH early in your shell rc. Example for zsh/bash:
```bash
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$PATH
# asdf (installed via brew)
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh || true
```
That usually fixes most "command not found" issues.

cal: fwiw if you're on fish it's different: `set -gx PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH`. Also asdf needs to be initialized — `asdf plugin-add python` then `asdf install python 3.11.6` and `asdf global python 3.11.6`.

infra-bot: Onboarding doc: <internal onboarding/dev-env.md> has the recommended snippets for zsh, bash, and fish + VS Code settings.

andre: +1 to using asdf for runtimes so you don't mix brew/python with pyenv or system. For Ruby please avoid rvm; we standardize on asdf + ruby plugin. No Rosetta normally unless you're using intel-only binaries (rare).

julie: hey @newhire_tom — if you want I can dump my company-starter dotfiles (zsh, env vars, gitconfig) to a gist you can clone. saves a few headaches. :rocket:

newhire_tom: thanks everyone! quick follow-up: I used pyenv previously — should I uninstall it? also any notes on pipx + brew python coexisting? I don't want to break tooling.

lena: If you switch to asdf, uninstalling pyenv is cleaner to avoid PATH collisions. For pipx, install it into the asdf-managed python: `pip install --user pipx` then `pipx ensurepath`. Or use the brew `pipx` pkg but ensure path order puts asdf python first.

cal: when things look wrong run these and paste outputs: `which python`, `python -V`, `asdf current`, `brew --prefix asdf`, `echo $PATH`. Also check `~/.zprofile` vs `~/.zshrc` — login vs interactive can bite you.

newhire_tom: will try the snippets now and paste output if I hit errors. Thanks for the speedy help — appreciate it! :)

julie: welcome again! if you want the dotfiles link ping me and I'll @ you when it's up.
